newsitem.title: USA: Kansas harvest, sowing advance with dry weather.
newsitem.headline: Kansas harvest, sowing advance with dry weather.

text.p: Dry weather during the week ended Sunday allowed Kansas farmers to continue seeding and fall harvesting, the weekly state crop report said.

"Fall harvest continues, but in some cases farmers are waiting for grain to dry to acceptable moisture levels," the report said. "There has been no widespread frost to date.... (but) at this point a frost would be beneficial as it would halt growth and and aid in the drying process."
Wheat seeding was 94 percent complete, on par with average but lagging 95 percent a year ago. Wheat was 74 percent emerged, versus 69 last year and the average of 70 percent.
Wheat was rated 88 percent good to excellent and 12 fair.
Corn was 70 percent harvested versus 57 percent last year and the average of 74 percent. Corn was rated 86 percent good to excellent, versus 84 percent at that level a week ago.
Sorghum was 45 percent harvested, versus 54 a year ago and the average of 51 percent. Sorghum was 93 percent mature, versus 93 a year ago and 90 on average.
Sorghum was rated 87 percent good to excellent, versus 87 percent at that level a week ago.
Soybeans were rated 85 percent good to excellent, versus 83 at that level a week ago. Sixty-one percent of soybeans were harvested, versus 64 last year and 65 on average.
Pasture condition was rated 73 percent good to excellent, versus 75 at that level last week.
